query: For a multicomponent high-entropy alloy in its high-temperature solid and liquid states, what single intervention could overcome the limited accuracy, availability, and efficiency of determining melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change upon melting, and liquid thermodynamic properties across a large compositional space? Formulate one hypothesis that states the intervention and causal mechanism, predicts the outcome relative to current experimental and computational baselines, defines the applicable composition and temperature ranges, identifies supporting prior evidence, and proposes a decisive falsification test against independent reference data.

Paper node: Phase prediction and experimental realisation of a new high entropy alloy using machine learning (2023). Cited 7 times before the cutoff; 0 papers in this graph say something specific about it.
Own digest: Paper card. Question: Can machine learning reliably predict the crystal structure (FCC, BCC, FCC+BCC, MIP) of high-entropy alloys (HEAs) synthesized via melting and casting routes without using synthetic data augmentation, and is synthetic data augmentation a reliable practice for this domain?. System: High-entropy alloys (HEAs) comprising 30 elements (Al, Co, Cr, Fe, Ni, Cu, Mn, Ti, V, Nb, Mo, Zr, Hf, Ta, W, C, Mg, Zn, Si, Re, N, Li, Sn, Be, B, Ag, Pt, Y, Pd, Au); specifically a novel alloy Ni25Cu18.75Fe25Co25Al6.25.. Processing: Vacuum arc melting of elemental buttons (Ni, Cu, Fe, Co, Al; purity > 99.99%) under high purity Ar environment, followed by multiple melting/solidification cycles for homogeneity, vacuum sealing in quartz tube, homogenization at 1000 °C for 10 h, and water quenching.. Test conditions: Machine learning models trained on 1200 experimental datasets from melting/casting routes; tested on 240 samples from original data and 279 samples from augmen
